feature: A long edit scrubs a refresh behind the hand, not two
summary: Dragging the playhead across the 6 minute reference edit now shows each picture one screen refresh after the hand in the middle of a drag, where it was two. Each picture of the edit draws in 4.2 ms, down from 5.6.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The 6 minute reference edit: Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh, then open it.

try.do: Drag the playhead slowly across the first minute and watch the picture keep up with your hand.
Hunt back and forth over one cut, quickly, and watch for the picture lagging behind.
Press Space to play through a dissolve and the cube transition.
Pause, pick a title and nudge it with the arrow keys: it should move at once.

evaluate: Does a slow drag of the playhead feel attached to your hand?
When you hunt over a cut, does the picture ever stay behind long enough to notice?
Do the colours and the picture look exactly as they did before while playing?
rough: Speed walk, worst of 3 runs each side (Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh): picture behind the hand in the middle, medium drag 2 -> 1 refresh, hunt 2 -> 1; composite median 5.6 -> 4.2 ms. At worst it is still 3 refreshes behind, against the bar of 1.
Playback still drops about 1 frame a minute (bar 0), and an edit while playing still holds the main thread 15 to 63 ms (bar 16). Both stay open on this task.
The sharp recording frame under a fast drag still arrives 30 to 40 refreshes after the hand in the middle: that is decoding, not drawing.
Export is untouched: it draws through its own path, which this change does not reach.
